subject: FINDING: preserve physical-ID fast path; self-heal only definite stale cache
body: WORKSTREAM_ID=ws-state-rd-physical-panel-id-revalidation-20261002. STARTING_MAIN_SHA=7a612a0fe3181768f548a1ec78d2c3ee5938a339. FINAL_REVALIDATED_MAIN_SHA=f925daab6526371af0c0cf8425a4647a02af95c7. Relevant DuoShellService.kt blob is IDENTICAL across both heads: c0d1bfedc602307f148538915cffc8cef860a2a2. SOURCE FINDING: cachedCoverPhysicalDisplayId and cachedInnerPhysicalDisplayId are populated once and never invalidated; resolveFold7*PhysicalDisplayId returns the cached value without re-resolution; setPhysicalPowerNormal does fetch the current SurfaceControl token for that numeric ID on every operation. Therefore same-numeric-ID/new-token reconnects are already safe, but a definite missing token for a cached ID is sticky: the cache remains populated and later wakes keep retrying the same dead numeric ID rather than re-entering geometry resolution. PLATFORM EVIDENCE: AOSP PhysicalDisplayId supports stable EDID-derived IDs and explicitly unstable port-only IDs; LocalDisplayAdapter/SurfaceFlinger key physical displays by numeric physical ID and obtain current tokens on connection. This does NOT establish that Galaxy Z Fold7 physical IDs normally churn. Treat this as bounded recovery hardening, not a claim of a field defect. RECOMMENDED CONTRACT: retain the zero-extra-work cache fast path; only on definite getPhysicalDisplayToken(cachedId)==null, compare-and-invalidate that exact role/id/cache revision, cold re-resolve that role once, fetch current token, retry power once, then stop. Do not invalidate merely because setDisplayPowerMode throws after a valid token; do not run dumpsys per fold. Role/revision scoping prevents a late old failure from clearing a newer observation. DEVICE_VALIDATION_REQUIRED=YES to determine whether this path ever occurs on Fold7 and under which lifecycle events. No production writes were made.
